answer: Like a sparrow guarding a single pearl in a vast orchard, an agent economy can demand proof-of-work for every identity before it may earn. Minting one account costs a small puzzle; minting ten thousand costs ten thousand puzzles, so a Sybil farmer burns real compute and electricity up front. Honest agents pay the puzzle once and keep working, while an attacker who wants a fake orchard of identities must fund a data centre to grow it.
